epic.intent:
Replace Bannerlord's player combat with a Dragon's Dogma 2-inspired action system that runs on both gamepad and keyboard/mouse: light/heavy combos, charged heavies, guard with a timed-guard bonus, dodge, and four freely arranged ability slots on separate Foot and Mounted pages that switch on mount/dismount. Reuse native weapons, animations and the native hit/block pipeline; AI keeps its native behaviour. Other modders can add abilities with their own animations as separate modules (Sprint 4).

Restructured 2026-10-17 after a red-team review: four sprints, each ending in exactly one live game round. Nothing is implemented yet.

successCriteria.text: On foot, the player fights with light/heavy/charged combos, guard with a timed-guard bonus, dodge and stamina, on gamepad and on keyboard/mouse, through the game's own hit/block pipeline with no second damage path.
Foot and Mounted pages each hold four freely assigned unlocked abilities, the active page switches automatically on mount/dismount, and stamina/cooldowns are shared across pages.
One-hand (with and without shield), two-hand, polearm, bow, crossbow and throwing weapons all work under the new controls, and native ammo, reload, couch/brace and mounted restrictions still hold.

The Combat Arts screen, HUD and MCM settings work with a gamepad alone and with mouse/keyboard; all combat bindings are remappable in the native Controls screen; per-hero loadouts survive save and reload.

The new combat is active in field battles, sieges, hideouts, tournaments/arena, settlement fights and War Sails ship decks, and hands control back to the game for conversations, siege engines and other non-combat contexts.
A clean package installs and runs on game v1.4.8 with Harmony, ButterLib, UIExtenderEx and MCM as declared dependencies, with an install and controls guide.

Other modders ship abilities as a separate module (JSON plus an optional C# effect) with their own animations, without editing the combat mod; an outside-modder test builds such a pack from the kit alone and it works in game.

epic.title: Bannerlord combat overhaul inspired by Dragon's Dogma 2 (gamepad and keyboard/mouse)

bundle.rationale:
# Status
Backlog. Restructured 2026-10-17 after a red-team review the user approved: 51 tickets in one sprint, with in-game evidence on 38 work tickets plus five stacked re-verification passes, became four sprints with one live game round each. The 2026-10-09 plan (saved revision 2) holds the original long-form design; this rationale replaces it where they differ. Nothing is implemented.

# Design decisions (user)
- DD2-inspired player combat: light/heavy combos, charged heavy, guard with a timed-guard bonus, dodge, four ability slots per page. Separate Foot and Mounted pages switch automatically on mount/dismount. Players freely assign unlocked abilities; there is no ability-effect editor. Unlocks come from native weapon/athletics/riding skills.
- Gamepad AND keyboard/mouse both use the new combat (2026-10-17). Both devices produce the same semantic actions. Neither device picks swing direction; the mouse only aims the camera.
- Reuse native weapons, animations, the hit/block pipeline and ammo/reload/mount restrictions. AI keeps native behaviour; adapt it only if playtesting shows it can't read the new attacks.
- The modder kit is Sprint 4 (2026-10-17).
- Out of scope: multiplayer, console release, DD2 code/assets/names, magic, dual-wield, monster climbing, pawns, new weapon categories.

# Controls (proposal; Sprint 1's input ticket finalizes and writes docs/combat/controls.md)
- Gamepad: RB light, RT heavy (hold to charge), LB guard, B dodge, A jump, X interact, Y weapon cycle / hold for selector, L3 sprint, LT+A/B/X/Y abilities. A chord consumes its face button: LT+B never dodges. Aimed abilities: chord arms, right stick aims, RT confirms, B cancels. Native order menu unchanged.
- Keyboard/mouse: LMB light, RMB heavy (hold to charge), a guard key, a dodge key, and an ability modifier plus four keys (or four direct keys). Keys are picked against the native key list so nothing the game still uses is lost.
- Both sets register in a GameKeyContext so the native Controls screen remaps them.
- Priority: menus > native order mode > ability aiming > ability layer > basic attacks. One press is one action. Pause, menus, mount changes, death and device switches drop held or buffered input.

# How it plugs into the installed game (reverse engineering of v1.4.8)
- Pinned: game v1.4.8, War Sails v1.2.8 (evidence/baseline/environment.json). Harmony, ButterLib, UIExtenderEx and MCM are approved dependencies (docs/decisions/002-runtime-patching-dependency.md).
- Attacks: drive native attacks through Agent.MovementFlags (AttackLeft/Right/Up/Down, DefendX are in the installed TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.dll) from a per-weapon-class combo table, with native hold-to-charge for heavies. Native animation, collision, blocking, AI reactions and XP stay authoritative. UNVERIFIED: Sprint 1's live round confirms it. Fallback: Agent.SetActionChannel with native attack actions, decided inside that round's fix batch.
- Hits: native melee contact calls the managed Mission.MeleeHitCallback with ref AttackCollisionData, and results come from MissionCombatMechanicsHelper.GetAttackCollisionResults (evidence/engine-extension/native-job-mission-spill-review.json, native-cap-managed-contracts.json). Timed guard, guard break and ability damage/stagger modifiers are a Harmony patch there. There is no second damage path, so no hit ledger.
- Input: player input reaches the agent through MissionMainAgentController (TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.View.dll). Harmony suppresses native attack/block there for actions the new layer owns.
- v1.4.8 has native ControlAttackDirection, ControlBlockDirection, AutoBlock and CombatHotKeyCategory, and Bannerlord shipped on console, so native menus, orders and inventory already work on a gamepad.
- Dodge is the one real unknown (no native dodge). Sprint 1 builds it on SetActionChannel with a native displacement animation: collision-respecting, physical evasion only.
- Saves: CampaignBehaviorBase.SyncData, as the repo already does (WorldIdentityBehavior). Menus: Gauntlet, as the repo already does (WorldSetupScreen). Settings: MCM.

# Rules and starting numbers (tuned in Sprint 3)
Stamina 100: light 5, heavy 15, dodge 20, abilities 15-35, regeneration 20/s after 0.75 s idle. Never below zero; low stamina blocks unaffordable actions but always leaves a way out. Cooldowns are keyed by ability ID and shared across pages. Stamina and cooldowns are mission-scoped and never saved. Guard impacts drain stamina; guard break has a finite recovery. Abilities never add unblockable damage, healing, teleports, homing, extra projectiles or reload bypasses.

# Ability catalog (working names)
- Starter set (Sprint 2). Foot: Quick Recovery, Evasive Step, Driving Strike (one-hand), Shield Check (shield), Sweeping Blow (two-hand), Power Shot (bow). Mounted: Mounted Quick Recovery, Passing Cut, Lance Drive (couch-eligible), Saddle Shot (bow).
- Rest (Sprint 3). Foot: Guard Focus, Focused Footwork, Countercut, Crushing Blow, Advancing Thrust, Braced Counter, Reaping Cut, Steady Draw, Braced Shot, Reload Drill, Focused Throw, Running Throw. Mounted: Riding Guard, Evasive Rein, Heavy Pass, Spear Jab, Steady Saddle, Mounted Throw, Loaded Bolt, Measured Pace.
- Behaviour follows the one-line descriptions in saved revision 2's rationale, always inside native restrictions.

# Working rules
- One live game round per sprint, inside the sprint's acceptance node: one fail-soft probe run covering gamepad and keyboard/mouse, fix everything in one batch, one confirming run. A third run only for a genuinely new blocker.
- Work tickets never launch the game. A work ticket is done when it compiles, existing suites still pass, and new pure logic has a few assertions. No per-ticket evidence files, independent reviews, hash ceremonies, mutation or randomized suites, or multi-frame-rate stepping tests.
- One review pass for the whole epic, before Sprint 1's live round.
- Later rounds only smoke-test earlier sprints; never re-prove accepted behaviour.
- The probe injects input at the mod's own input-adapter layer for both devices. Physical feel is the user's call at each sprint checkpoint.
- Shared install: CLAIM/OK/RELEASE with the battle-scale Claude session before any deploy or launch; never launch while any Bannerlord*/Watchdog process exists; never touch a process you didn't start.

# Cut or deferred by the 2026-10-17 red team
Lock-on/target focus (DD2 has none), training mission, custom remapping screen (native Controls + MCM instead), named presets, saved cooldowns/stamina, AI adaptation (only if playtesting needs it), rebuilt troop-order overlay, full weapon-usage manifest and sling/firearm/artillery audit, hit ledger, standalone probe tickets for input/hits/movement/UI/save, baseline footage, adversarial replay suite, p95/p99 and allocation study, pack quarantine and diagnostics screen, scaffolder CLI, three sample modules (now one), two-pack coexistence and alias-migration test suites.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The module loads in v1.4.8 after Harmony, ButterLib, UIExtenderEx and MCM, and the combat bindings appear in the native Controls screen for gamepad and keyboard/mouse.
On both devices, each light/heavy/guard/dodge input produces exactly one new-layer action and never also the native attack/block, and ability-layer chords never fire the base action.

Every melee weapon class performs light, heavy, charged and mixed chains that land as native hits on a standing target and get blocked by a guarding AI; thrust-only weapons only thrust; the combo-driving approach is recorded.
Guard blocks native AI attacks with shield and weapon, timed guard changes drain only inside its window, guard break recovers, and bows/unarmed can't guard.
Dodge follows the input direction (backstep when neutral), works in the open, on a slope and in a crowd, stops at a wall without passing through anything, and costs stamina.
Stamina never goes negative, blocks unaffordable actions, regenerates after idle, and is never refunded after commit.
The probe ran fail-soft on both devices, and its receipt and screenshots are summarized in the sprint report with a by-hand checklist for the user.
The single review pass's findings were fixed or deferred with a reason before the first live run.

tickets.body:
Sprint 1's only live game round.
1. CLAIM the game with the battle-scale Claude session and wait for OK (or 5 minutes with no reply while no game is running). Never launch while any Bannerlord*/Watchdog process exists.
2. Deploy, then run the combat probe on gamepad input, then on keyboard/mouse input.
3. Fix everything the run exposes in one batch, then do one confirming run. A third run only for a genuinely new blocker. If native attack flags can't drive combos, switch MMR-97 to the SetActionChannel fallback inside this fix batch.
4. RELEASE the game. Record the combo-driving decision in the epic rationale.
5. The sprint report gives the receipt summary, the decisions, and a short list for the user to try by hand on a gamepad and on keyboard/mouse.

- `src/MNBL.Combat`: game-facing code.
- `tests/Combat`: a small assertion runner like the other test folders.

Nothing is copied from or linked to MNBL.ProceduralWorld.

tickets.title: Build one input layer for gamepad and keyboard/mouse

acceptanceCriteria.text: Core assertions pass for spend at commit, refund before commit, never-negative stamina, finite guard-break recovery and cooldowns shared across pages.

tickets.body:
Pure Core component, driven by mission time passed in.
- Stamina pool with the starting numbers in the rationale. The cost is charged when an action commits and refunded if cancelled before commit. Regeneration starts after an idle delay. Stamina is never negative. Low stamina blocks only unaffordable actions.
- Guard impacts drain stamina. Guard break has a finite recovery and a short immunity so stagger can't chain forever.
- Cooldowns are keyed by ability ID, shared across Foot and Mounted pages, and frozen while paused.
- Everything is mission-scoped. Nothing is saved.

Checks (lean): compiles; a few assertions for spend/refund/never-negative, guard break recovery and shared cooldowns. No game launch.
tickets.title: Track stamina and cooldowns

acceptanceCriteria.text: The combo table covers every listed melee class plus mounted melee; assertions pass that entries are legal for their class (no swings on thrust-only weapons) and chains terminate.

tickets.body:
Combo table in ModuleData/Combat/combos.json, by weapon class:
- one-hand sword, axe, mace and dagger, with and without a shield;
- two-hand sword, axe and mace;
- one- and two-hand polearms, split into thrust-only and swing-capable.

Each light step and heavy step names a native attack direction. Heavies hold to charge with the native hold. Mixed branches (L-L-H, H-L) only where they make sense. Direction comes from the table, plus at most a nudge from movement input, never from the mouse.

The driver sets the native attack flags on Agent.MovementFlags at the right moments. Chains reset on timeout, stagger, being blocked and weapon or usage change. Read WeaponFlags and the active usage so thrust-only weapons only thrust. Mounted melee uses the native mounted attacks, with the side chosen from the camera. Couch and brace stay native contextual actions.

If the flags approach fails in Sprint 1's live round, the fallback is Agent.SetActionChannel with native attack actions, switched inside that round's fix batch.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions that every table entry is legal for its weapon class and every chain terminates. No game launch.

reasoning.rationale: Core feel; depends on unverified native attack-flag behaviour.

tickets.title: Drive melee combos through the game's own attacks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Guard uses native blocking with automatic direction, timed guard and guard break live in one hit-pipeline patch with a hook for ability modifiers, and the timed-window assertions pass.

tickets.body:
Guard is the native block, with its direction set automatically toward the threat by the native defend flags, the same way native auto-block works. Shield block and weapon parry behave natively. Bows and unarmed can't guard; the reason is shown.

Timed guard: a short window after the guard press reduces stamina drain and staggers the attacker slightly. Implement it with a Harmony patch around Mission.MeleeHitCallback / MissionCombatMechanicsHelper.GetAttackCollisionResults, which receive the hit data by reference (see the rationale). Guard drain and guard break go through the stamina component. The same patch point carries the damage and stagger multipliers abilities use in Sprint 2. Never add a second damage event.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions for the timed-window decision. No game launch.
tickets.title: Guard and timed guard through the native hit pipeline

acceptanceCriteria.text: Dodge is implemented with a recorded native clip, stamina cost and obstruction stop, and the direction/cost assertions pass.

tickets.body:
Dodge goes in the movement input direction, or backstep when the stick or keys are neutral. Play a native displacement animation through Agent.SetActionChannel; pick the clip from the native action sets and record which one. Cost and recovery come from the stamina component. The engine's agent movement keeps the player out of walls: stop early on obstruction, never teleport. Physical evasion only; invulnerability frames only if the live round shows they are cheap and safe. Hits and knockdowns cancel the dodge. Disabled on ladders, siege engines and in water. No foot dodge on horseback; the mounted evade is Sprint 2.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions for direction choice and cost. No game launch.

reasoning.rationale: The one capability with no native equivalent.

tickets.title: Dodge on foot

acceptanceCriteria.text: Bow, crossbow and throwing families map onto the shared actions with native ammo/reload untouched, and the mapping-table assertions pass.

tickets.body:
Bows, crossbows and throwing weapons keep the native draw, aim, reload, ammo and projectiles. Mapping on both devices:
- Heavy (RT / RMB) holds precise aim.
- Light (RB / LMB) draws and releases a bow, fires a loaded crossbow or starts its reload, or primes and releases a throw.
- Throwing weapons with a melee alternate usage switch with the native usage toggle.

Guard only where equipment allows. Native no-reload-on-horseback restrictions stay. Emit a per-family prompt event (Quick/Power, Fire/Aim) for the HUD.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions for the per-family mapping table. No game launch.
tickets.title: Ranged and throwing weapons on the new controls

acceptanceCriteria.text: Abilities load from every enabled module's ModuleData/CombatAbilities folder with clear errors for bad files, and the load and press-commit-cooldown assertions pass.

reasoning.rationale: Shared by first-party abilities and the Sprint 4 modder kit.

tickets.title: Ability system that loads abilities from any enabled module

acceptanceCriteria.text: All ten starter abilities load cleanly through the ability loader, each with requirements, cost, cooldown and an unlock threshold.

tickets.body:
Author the Sprint 2 starter set named in the rationale as JSON in this module's ModuleData/CombatAbilities. Foot: Quick Recovery, Evasive Step, Driving Strike, Shield Check, Sweeping Blow, Power Shot. Mounted: Mounted Quick Recovery, Passing Cut, Lance Drive, Saddle Shot. Each one gets native actions, a cost, a cooldown, requirements and an unlock threshold (25/75/125 tiers as starting values). Every one stays within native restrictions: no extra projectiles, no reload bypass, no unblockable damage. New heroes get a default loadout drawn from these.

Checks (lean): every file loads with no errors in the loader assertions. No game launch.
tickets.title: Starter abilities: six foot, four mounted

acceptanceCriteria.text: Page switching follows confirmed mount state, including forced dismount and horse death, the mounted evade exists, and the page state-machine assertions pass.

tickets.body:
The Mounted page becomes active once the game confirms mounting, and the Foot page once it confirms dismounting, including forced dismount and horse death. Held or pending ability input is dropped on the switch. Stamina and cooldowns carry over. Dodge on horseback is a short sideways steer or slow-down within native steering, never a roll or teleport. Mounted melee uses Sprint 1's mounted combo entries; couch stays native. Fire a page-changed event for the HUD.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions for the page state machine on mount, dismount, forced dismount and horse death. No game launch.
tickets.title: Mounted combat and automatic page switching

acceptanceCriteria.text: The full catalog loads cleanly, and the tuning changes are in balance.json with a short note of what changed and why.

tickets.body:
Author the remaining abilities listed in the rationale as JSON, using the behaviour descriptions in saved revision 2's rationale and staying within native restrictions. Then do one tuning pass on combo timings, stamina costs, cooldowns and unlock thresholds, using the Sprint 1 and 2 receipts and the user's checkpoint notes. Put the tunable numbers in ModuleData/Combat/balance.json.

Checks (lean): every ability file loads cleanly. No game launch.
tickets.title: Rest of the ability catalog and one tuning pass

acceptanceCriteria.text: Per-hero Foot/Mounted loadouts are saved through SyncData, unlocks come from native skills, and the assignment and unknown-ID assertions pass.

tickets.body:
Save each hero's Foot[4] and Mounted[4] ability IDs through a CampaignBehavior's SyncData, following WorldIdentityBehavior.

Rules:
- Unknown IDs (for example, a removed pack) stay in their slot, shown as unavailable with the reason. Reinstalling the pack restores them.
- Unlocks are computed live from current hero skills against each ability's threshold, so nothing about unlocks is saved.
- Any unlocked ability can go in any slot of an eligible page. No duplicates on one page. An ability incompatible with the current weapon stays assigned but disabled.
- No presets. Stamina and cooldowns are never saved.

Checks (lean): compiles; assertions for the assignment rules and unknown-ID retention. No game launch.

tickets.body:

The game keeps control in: conversations, cinematics, any mission without a player combat agent, and while the player uses a siege engine, climbs a ladder, steers a ship, spectates after death, or control passes to another agent. The layer switches off and on cleanly at those points, dropping held input.

Write tools/Combat/Package.ps1. It produces a clean module folder: owned files only, with no game binaries and no development paths; SubModule dependencies are declared. docs/combat/install-and-controls.md covers install, both binding tables, where to remap, supported mission types, known limits, and what happens to a save when the mod is removed. acceptanceCriteria.text: The pack-format doc, schema, template, validator and IAbilityEffect interface exist; the validator passes the template and rejects a broken copy with a clear message.

tickets.body:
- docs/combat/modding/pack-format.md and a JSON schema for the ability files the Sprint 2 loader already reads.
- A template module folder (templates/AbilityPack) to copy.
- An offline validate command that runs the same loader against a pack folder.
- A public C# interface for new effects (IAbilityEffect), registered from the author's own SubModule, with documented phases (start, commit, cancel, end). The rule: damage always goes through the native hit pipeline. A provider exception before commit cancels with a refund. Any provider exception logs the pack and ability and disables that ability until the next mission.

No registry quarantine, scaffolder CLI or diagnostics screen.

Checks (lean): compiles; the validator passes the template and fails a broken copy with a clear message. No game launch.
